content:
Irrigation equipment insurance and crop insurance answer different questions. A damaged pump creates a repair bill; an interrupted watering cycle may affect a crop under separate conditions. A farmer in Moldova should prepare both questions before the 2027 irrigation season rather than assume one policy protects the whole production chain.

Editorial revision: 26 November 2026. Planning material for 2027; the scenarios below are hypothetical, not incident or demand forecasts.

Which farms need this assessment?

It is useful for growers operating pumping stations, pivots, reels, drip systems or shared irrigation installations. Identify equipment owned by the farm, rented equipment and infrastructure operated by another organization. The name of a field does not establish ownership of every pipe and electrical component serving it.

Map the system into pumping, filtration, distribution, controls and power supply. Record movable equipment's operating sites, transport and off-season storage. An inventory limited to the farm office address does not explain where a mobile pump is actually exposed.

Damage scenarios and contractual exclusions

Ask how a proposal treats accidental mechanical breakdown, electrical damage, theft, fire and relevant natural events. MOLDASIG's agricultural page lists irrigation equipment among its categories (checked 25 November 2026). This is a local category example, not acceptance of this farm or every event.

Request explicit answers about corrosion, wear, freezing, maintenance, known defects and damage during movement. Lack of water at the source is not the same as physical damage to the system. Ask separately whether any crop consequence can be assessed and under which product, event and period.

A practical 2027 readiness scenario

Imagine the main pump stopping during a critical watering period. This is an operational exercise, not a drought prediction. Establish who can diagnose the cause safely, where compatible parts can be sourced and whether a temporary pump can actually serve the required area.

For a system expanded in stages, compare the old inventory with new filters, controllers and served plots. Record changes before renewal and ask whether insurer notification or amendments are needed. A new invoice does not automatically amend the insurance contract.

What can the farm prevent more effectively?

Before the season, ask the responsible service team to review unresolved leaks, electrical warnings and preservation records for stored equipment. Check whether an identified replacement part is compatible and actually available. This is a prevention checklist, not an instruction to alter settings or bypass protective devices.

How much could irrigation insurance cost?

No farm-specific or confirmed 2027 tariff is published here. Request a calculation based on component values, age and condition, operating sites, protections requested and seasonal use. Distinguish the premium, meaning the policy price, from the deductible retained by the insured in a claim. (BNM: contract terms, checked 25 November 2026; general guidance, not individual policy conditions.)

Compare the same assets, limits and period. A low quote for a pump alone cannot be compared directly with one considering distribution equipment. Ask about transport, fitting and expedited replacement expenses rather than adding them to an expected payment without confirmation.

Prepare the file before watering starts

Gather equipment records, ownership or lease documents, maintenance reports, known issues and dated replacement estimates. For crop questions, add plots, crop type and season separately. The crop and drought insurance preparation guide addresses a different object from repairing the pump. AIPA's agricultural-insurance information, checked on 25 November 2026, points to the support framework. It does not verify 2027 eligibility, procedures, funds or an individual approval. Do not subtract an assumed subsidy from the budget as a certainty.

Three situations: what to compare before deciding

The MOLDASIG agricultural page, rechecked on 26 November 2026, names irrigation systems among equipment. This does not establish locations, movement conditions or crop-loss consequences for a particular system.

  • Fixed station: compare the pump, power supply and distribution equipment with the declared list. Prepare ownership, service and value records. Confirm named objects rather than treating every component serving the field as one insured machine.
  • Mobile pump at two fields or in winter storage: compare operating, transport and storage locations. Prepare the movement plan and inventory. Check territory and update procedure before relying on the address of only one field.
  • Pump stops and a crop suffers: compare technical failure with the agronomic cause of crop damage. Retain service findings and crop records separately. Ask which policy, if any, considers each consequence; an equipment entry does not establish crop protection.

Frequently asked questions

What information is needed to calculate the irrigation premium?

Use a component list with supported values, operating sites, season, condition and requested protections. State where movable equipment is used and stored. Compare proposals for the same pumps, distribution and controls, and read deductible and expense limits. A price for one pumping station does not establish the cost of the whole irrigation system.

What documents should the farm gather before the season?

Prepare equipment and ownership records, leases where applicable, maintenance reports, known issues and dated replacement information. Link each important component to its operating or storage site. For crop questions, supply plots, crop type and season separately; the equipment inventory does not describe the entire harvest exposure.

How should we document a pump stoppage?

Record when the stoppage was noticed, observed symptoms and the person arranging competent inspection. Keep findings, relevant service records and expenses distinct from initial assumptions. Follow safety instructions and the policy notification procedure. Do not repeatedly restart unsafe equipment or diagnose an electrical cause merely to fit a preferred insurance description.

Will equipment insurance reimburse the affected crop?

Ask for a separate contractual answer. Repairing a pump and calculating crop loss involve different objects and evidence. Explain the dependency and the actual cause, then check whether an eligible solution exists for each consequence. An accepted repair expense does not by itself establish payment for the crop or lost sales.

Does cover follow a mobile pump to another plot?

Check the stated locations, territory, transport and notification arrangements before relying on it at the new site. Retain the updated inventory and insurer reply. An unchanged serial number or internal transfer record does not prove that the policy accepts every new location or movement.
